expect_red: closing the flyout puts the page back exactly -- the nav rail, the DAG pane's box and the drawing's box all as they were

mutations.contract: Closing the panel puts the page back exactly. The shift comes off in the dialog's own `close` handler, which is the one seam every close path goes through.
mutations.note: Now that the page yields room rather than being covered, "closing restores whatever it covered" stopped being true by construction and became a real claim with a real way to get it wrong -- a page left shifted with no panel on it. The mutation guards the handler on `nodes.flyout.open`, which reads as a sensible "only if it was open" check and is in fact dead on arrival: by the time `close` fires the dialog's `open` is already false, so the class never comes off on ANY close path. What reddens is the width comparison after the ✕, and the same failure is what wiring the removal to the button instead of to the dialog would produce on every other path. Kept narrow deliberately: removing the handler altogether would strand the page for the checks that follow and take the suite down as an error rather than a named failure. Re-aimed (2026-10-28, the_kinematic_study_reads_like_every_other_study_and_its_plot_shows_both_tolerances): the old mutation kept `flyout-open` after a close, which showed only while that class also stood the preview pane down; with the stand-down retired it removes one hairline. This one lays the closed scene out anyway, so the DAG's box does not go back.
